issues.legal_issue: Time spent prosecuting an earlier proceeding may be excluded when calculating limitation for a later suit seeking the same claim, where the earlier court could not adjudicate that claim because of a defect analogous to a jurisdictional defect.
material_facts: A claim for future mesne profits was included in an earlier money suit, and the trial court decreed that claim.
On appeal, the decree for future mesne profits was set aside because such relief could not be granted in a pure money suit.
The later suit sought damages for a period that included the period covered by the disallowed claim in the earlier suit.
The claim in the later suit was founded on the same cause of action as the earlier claim, and the earlier suit had been prosecuted in good faith and with due diligence.
The trial court had made an effective decree for the future mesne profits, and the appellate court set it aside without adjudicating the merits of that claim.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff was entitled under section 14(1) of the Limitation Act, 1908, to exclude the time during which the earlier suit was prosecuted when calculating limitation for the later suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1) of the Limitation Act, 1908 permits exclusion of time spent prosecuting, with due diligence and in good faith, an earlier civil proceeding founded on the same cause of action where the earlier court was unable to entertain it because of a jurisdictional defect or another cause of a like nature. That expression is to be construed liberally. Under the approach in Jaikishan Singh v. The Peoples Bank of Northern India, the defect must prevent the court from entertaining the proceeding or deciding it on the merits; under Shrimati Nrityamoni Dassi v. Lakhan Chandra Sen, an effective decree capable of enforcement until set aside may support deduction of the earlier litigation period. Makhan Lal Madak v. Girish Chandra Jana was referred to in considering whether the earlier claim was wholly misconceived. The majority did not rely on the general principle discussed in Narayan Jivaji Patil v. Khandappagauda Patil. Hegde J., concurring in the result, considered section 14(1) inapplicable on its terms but applied the principle in Mst. Ranee Surno Moyee v. Shooshee Mukhee that setting aside an earlier satisfaction, including a decree, gives rise to a new cause of action.

rule.if: later_suit_seeks_same_claim and earlier_proceeding_was_civil and earlier_proceeding_same_cause and earlier_proceeding_good_faith_due_diligence and ((earlier_decree_effective_until_set_aside and earlier_decree_set_aside) or earlier_bar_prevented_merits_decision)

predicates.later_suit_seeks_same_claim: The claimant brought a later suit seeking the claim, or the same relief, that had been pursued in the earlier proceeding.
predicates.earlier_proceeding_was_civil: The claimant pursued the claim in an earlier civil proceeding against the opposing party.
predicates.earlier_proceeding_same_cause: The earlier proceeding and the later suit were founded on the same cause of action.
predicates.earlier_proceeding_good_faith_due_dilige: The claimant prosecuted the earlier proceeding in good faith and with due diligence.
predicates.earlier_decree_effective_until_set_aside: The earlier court issued a decree granting the claim that remained effective until it was set aside.
predicates.earlier_decree_set_aside: A later court set aside the earlier decree granting the claim.
predicates.earlier_bar_prevented_merits_decision: A defect in the earlier proceeding prevented the court from entertaining the claim or deciding it on the merits.
predicates.earlier_proceeding_time_excluded_from_li: The time spent prosecuting the earlier proceeding is excluded when calculating limitation for the later suit.

issues.definition: When a claimant diligently and in good faith pursues the same claim in an earlier civil proceeding and that proceeding either produces a decree later set aside or is stopped by a defect that prevents a decision on the merits, the time spent in that proceeding is excluded from the limitation calculation for the later suit.
